programs.name: sudlmo
programs.purpose: Apply frequency-dependent dynamic linear moveout correction to surface-wave traces.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUDLMO -- Dynamic Linear Move Out Correction for Surface Waves

params.name: dt
params.default: computed: first trace header dt divided by 1000000
params.description: Sample interval in seconds; an error occurs if the resulting value is zero.

params.name: invert
params.description: Use the inverse phase shift when nonzero.

params.name: cm
params.description: Divide the absolute offset by 100 when equal to 1.

params.name: cdp
params.default: computed: first trace header cdp

params.name: vnmo
params.description: Velocity values; repeat once per CDP when cdp is specified.

params.name: fnmo
params.description: Frequencies corresponding to vnmo; repeat once per CDP when cdp is specified.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: FFT and complex exponential depend on floating-point arithmetic. The FFT of a trace is computed only when its offset differs from the first trace's offset or its CDP changes; oldoffset and oldcdp are never updated, so traces matching the first offset can reuse stale transformed data. On a CDP change, interpolation uses nt rather than nf and can access outside the allocated arrays.
programs.difficulty_reason: It combines FFT phase shifts with frequency and CDP interpolation.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sudlmo vnmo=400 dt=0.004

test_cases.description: Inverse correction with a dispersive velocity function and centimeter offsets.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sudlmo vnmo=300,500 fnmo=0,40 invert=1 cm=1 dt=0.004

programs.license_note: Credits BRGM's Adnand Bitri and says the program is based on sufrac.

programs.name: suilog
programs.purpose: Reverse a logarithmic time-axis stretch using reconstruction parameters.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUILOG -- time axis inverse log-stretch of seismic traces

params.name: ntmin
params.description: Original minimum sample index used for the log stretch.

params.name: dt
params.description: Original header sample interval in microseconds, as written by sulog.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: The coordinate calculation uses log and float arithmetic; interpolation accumulates two products. dt is assigned directly to the integer trace header.
programs.difficulty_reason: It precomputes a nonlinear coordinate mapping and linear interpolation weights.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sulog ntmin=12 m=2 outpar=logpar > in.su && suilog par=logpar < in.su
suspike nt=128 ntr=4 | sulog ntmin=16 ntau=256 outpar=logpar > in.su && suilog par=logpar < in.su

programs.name: sulog
programs.purpose: Stretch the time axis of seismic traces logarithmically and write inverse parameters.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SULOG -- time axis log-stretch of seismic traces

params.name: ntmin
params.default: computed: 0.1 times first trace ns, converted to int

params.name: outpar
params.default: /dev/tty

params.name: m
params.description: Multiplier used to calculate the unpadded stretched length and sample interval.

params.name: ntau
params.default: computed: smallest power of 2 at least m times first trace ns

programs.float_sensitive_notes: log and exp determine interpolation coordinates; the stretched interval is converted to an integer microsecond header value. Small nt can make the default ntmin zero.
programs.difficulty_reason: It precomputes a nonlinear coordinate mapping and linear interpolation weights.

test_cases.description: Use a specified minimum sample and output parameter file.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sulog ntmin=12 outpar=logpar
suspike nt=128 ntr=4 | sulog ntmin=16 m=2 ntau=256 outpar=logpar

programs.name: sunmo
programs.purpose: Apply or approximately invert normal moveout using velocity functions of time and CDP.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUNMO - NMO for an arbitrary velocity function of time and CDP

params.name: tnmo
params.description: Velocity-function times; repeat for each specified CDP.

params.name: vnmo
params.description: NMO velocities; repeat for each specified CDP.

params.name: cdp
params.default: computed: first trace header cdp

params.name: sscale
params.description: Apply stretch amplitude scaling when nonzero.

params.name: invert
params.description: Perform approximate inverse NMO when nonzero.

params.name: upward
params.description: Select the upward mute scan when nonzero.

params.name: voutfile
params.description: Optional binary interpolated velocity output file.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Velocity interpolation, square roots, stretch derivatives, sinc interpolation and inverse mapping depend on floating-point rounding and operation order.
programs.difficulty_reason: It interpolates velocity functions across time and CDP and supports forward and inverse resampling.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sunmo tnmo=0,0.4 vnmo=1500,2000 smute=2 lmute=8
suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sunmo vnmo=1800 invert=1 sscale=0 upward=1

programs.name: sunmo_a
programs.purpose: Apply or approximately invert NMO with optional anisotropic moveout coefficients.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUNMO_a - NMO for an arbitrary velocity function of time and CDP with

params.name: tnmo
params.description: Velocity and anisotropy function times, repeated per CDP.

params.name: anis1
params.default: 0.0 for each velocity
params.description: First anisotropy coefficient, repeated per CDP.

params.name: anis2
params.default: 0.0 for each velocity
params.description: Second anisotropy coefficient, repeated per CDP.

params.name: cdp
params.default: computed: first trace header cdp

params.name: upward
params.description: Scan upward for the mute boundary.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Anisotropic quartic moveout, square roots, interpolation and inverse mapping are sensitive to rounding; invalid anisotropy can cause explicit errors.
programs.difficulty_reason: It extends forward and inverse NMO with interpolated anisotropy functions.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sunmo_a tnmo=0,0.4 vnmo=1500,2000 anis1=0,0 anis2=0,0 smute=2

test_cases.description: Inverse correction with non-default mute and scaling.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sunmo_a vnmo=1800 invert=1 sscale=0 lmute=8 upward=1

programs.name: sunmocsv
programs.purpose: Apply or approximately invert NMO using command-line or Q-file velocity functions on a 2D or 3D grid.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUNMOCSV - NMO for an arbitrary velocity function of time and 3D or 2D CDP

params.name: qin
params.description: Q-file containing velocity functions; otherwise cdp, tnmo and vnmo are required.

params.name: cdp
params.description: Velocity function CDPs; required when qin is absent.

params.name: tnmo
params.description: Velocity function times; required when qin is absent; repeat or supply one shared array.

params.name: vnmo
params.description: Velocity arrays; required once per CDP when qin is absent.

params.name: grid_xa
params.description: Grid corner A world X; required with a complete command-line grid.

params.name: grid_ya
params.description: Grid corner A world Y; required with a complete command-line grid.

params.name: grid_xb
params.description: Grid corner B world X; required with a complete command-line grid.

params.name: grid_yb
params.description: Grid corner B world Y; required with a complete command-line grid.

params.name: grid_xc
params.description: Grid corner C world X; required with a complete command-line grid.

params.name: grid_yc
params.description: Grid corner C world Y; required with a complete command-line grid.

params.name: grid_wb
params.description: Grid cell width along B; required with a complete command-line grid.

params.name: grid_wc
params.description: Grid cell width along C; required with a complete command-line grid.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Velocity input and interpolation mix double and float, use sorting and bilinear interpolation, and feed square-root moveout and sinc interpolation. Grid rounding uses lrint and can depend on the rounding mode.
programs.difficulty_reason: It combines Q-file parsing, 2D or 3D grid handling, velocity sorting and interpolation, and forward and inverse NMO.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sunmocsv cdp=1 tnmo=0,0.4 vnmo=1500,2000 smute=2

test_cases.description: Inverse NMO with output velocity file.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sunmocsv cdp=1 tnmo=0,0.4 vnmo=1500,2000 invert=1 sscale=0 voutfile=vel.bin

programs.name: sureduce
programs.purpose: Shift each trace to reduced time using its offset and a reducing velocity.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUREDUCE - convert traces to display in reduced time

params.name: dt
params.default: computed: first trace header dt divided by 1000000
params.description: Required when the first header dt is zero, but the supplied value is immediately overwritten with the zero header value.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Offset-to-sample conversion uses floating-point division and NINT. If header dt is zero, the code overwrites the required dt argument with zero and divides by zero.
programs.difficulty_reason: It computes an integer sample shift and copies or zero-fills each trace.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sureduce rv=8
suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sureduce rv=4

programs.name: suresamp
programs.purpose: Resample seismic or non-seismic traces onto a new regular time axis.

params.name: dt_in
params.default: computed: first trace dt/1000000 for seismic data or d1 for non-seismic data
params.description: Read only if the header input interval is zero; an error occurs if the resulting interval is zero.

params.name: rf
params.description: Resampling factor; zero means no factor-based change.

params.name: nt
params.default: computed: NINT(input ns times rf) if rf is nonzero, otherwise input ns

params.name: dt
params.default: computed: input interval divided by rf if rf is nonzero, otherwise input interval

params.name: tmin
params.default: computed: first trace delrt/1000 for seismic data or f1 for non-seismic data

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Sinc interpolation and repeated float addition of output coordinates affect exact samples; the seismic dt header is rounded to integer microseconds.
programs.difficulty_reason: It constructs a new sample grid and uses sinc interpolation for each trace.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | suresamp rf=2 verbose=1

test_cases.description: Set a new interval, count and start time.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=128 ntr=4 | suresamp nt=64 dt=0.008 tmin=0.016

programs.name: sushift
programs.purpose: Window and pad traces to a common time range.

params.name: dt
params.default: computed: first trace header dt

params.name: tmin
params.default: computed: first trace delrt divided by 1000

params.name: tmax
params.default: computed: output start time plus first trace ns times dt
params.description: Exclusive output end time in seconds.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Time bounds are rounded to integer microseconds; the output sample count is stored in an unsigned short before its maximum-size check.
programs.difficulty_reason: It copies an integer-aligned window and fills samples outside the input.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sushift tmin=0.04 tmax=0.3

test_cases.description: Pad a window with a nonzero value.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=128 ntr=4 | sushift dt=4000 tmin=-0.04 tmax=0.6 fill=2 verbose=1

programs.name: sutaupnmo
programs.purpose: Apply NMO to tau-p traces using velocity functions of tau and CDP.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUTAUPNMO - NMO for an arbitrary velocity function of tau and CDP

params.name: tnmo
params.description: Tau values corresponding to velocities; repeat per CDP.

params.name: cdp
params.default: computed: first trace header cdp

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Velocity interpolation, square roots, stretch derivatives and sinc interpolation depend on float rounding and operation order.
programs.difficulty_reason: It interpolates velocity functions and resamples traces according to tau-p moveout.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sutaup dx=25 option=2 pmin=0 pmax=0.0004 | sutaupnmo vnmo=1800 smute=2
suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sutaup dx=25 option=2 pmin=0 pmax=0.0004 | sutaupnmo tnmo=0,0.4 vnmo=1500,2000 lmute=8 sscale=0

programs.name: sutsq
programs.purpose: Resample traces between time and time-squared coordinates.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUTSQ -- time axis time-squared stretch of seismic traces

params.name: tmin
params.default: computed: 0.1 times first trace ns times header dt in seconds

params.name: flag
params.description: One selects forward transform; any other value selects inverse.

params.name: dt
params.description: Read only for inverse transformation. The code mistakenly stores a supplied value in the input interval variable and leaves output dt at zero.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Square roots and sinc interpolation are platform-sensitive. Explicit inverse dt leaves dtout zero, causing division by zero and invalid output size.
programs.difficulty_reason: It computes nonlinear coordinates and uses sinc interpolation for forward or inverse resampling.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sutsq flag=1 tmin=0.08

test_cases.description: Forward and inverse stretch using the inverse default interval.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=128 ntr=4 | sutsq flag=1 tmin=0.08 | sutsq flag=-1

programs.name: suttoz
programs.purpose: Resample time-domain traces onto a depth axis using interval velocity.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUTTOZ - resample from time to depth

params.name: vfile
params.description: Binary file of one velocity float per input time sample; overrides t and v.

params.name: dz
params.default: computed: minimum velocity times input dt divided by 2

params.name: fz
params.default: computed: first velocity times first trace delrt in seconds divided by 2

params.name: nz
params.default: computed: 1+(nt-1)*dt*vmax/(2*dz), converted to int

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Sequential integration of velocity, inverse mapping and sinc interpolation are rounding-sensitive. Extrapolation loops lack explicit array bounds and can overrun for unsuitable output ranges.
programs.difficulty_reason: It integrates and inverts a velocity function and resamples with sinc interpolation.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | suttoz v=1500 dz=3 nz=128
suspike nt=128 ntr=4 | suttoz t=0,0.4 v=1500,2000 dz=3 fz=0 nz=150 verbose=1

programs.name: suztot
programs.purpose: Resample depth-domain traces onto a time axis using interval velocity.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUZTOT - resample from depth to time

params.name: dz
params.default: computed: first trace header d1

params.name: vfile
params.description: Binary file of one velocity float per input depth sample; overrides z and v.

params.name: dt
params.default: computed: 2*dz/minimum velocity

params.name: ft
params.description: First output time; the code computes the default from initially zero ft, not fz.

params.name: nt
params.default: computed: 1+(nz-1)*dz*2/(dt*vmax), converted to int

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Sequential integration of reciprocal velocity, inverse mapping and sinc interpolation are rounding-sensitive. Extrapolation loops lack explicit array bounds; the final extrapolation formula uses output last time in its base term.
programs.difficulty_reason: It integrates and inverts a velocity function and resamples with sinc interpolation.

test_cases.description: Convert constant-velocity depth traces back to time.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | suttoz v=1500 dz=3 nz=128 | suztot v=1500 dt=0.004 nt=128
suspike nt=128 ntr=4 | suttoz v=1500 dz=3 nz=128 | suztot z=0,300 v=1500,1800 dt=0.004 ft=0 fz=0 nt=128 verbose=1

programs.license_note: Credits John Stockwell and states that the program is based on suttoz.c by Dave Hale.
